verdict.rationale: Pylon documents its own control over which issues the AI agent touches: the agent works only on issues assigned to it, which gives "full control of which customer issues your AI agent interacts with." There is no documented way to mark topics such as legal threats, cancellations or security as human-only so the agent is automatically blocked from them. Scoping is per-assignment, and natural-language runbooks are only soft guidance, not a hard guardrail. Missing for 10: topic- or category-based human-only exclusion rules, guaranteed enforcement that the agent never responds on flagged topics, automatic handoff to humans when such topics are detected, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a support ops lead, I mark topics as human-only — legal threats, cancellations, security — and the agent never freelances on them

citations.quote: This means you have full control of which customer issues your AI agent interacts with.
You can also assign an individual issue to your AI agent, the same way you might normally assign an issue to a team member.
